original_value: The fast detection of pigs is a crucial aspect for a surveillance environment intended for the ultimate purpose of the 24 h tracking of individual pigs. Particularly, in a realistic pig farm environment, one should consider various illumination conditions such as sunlight, but such consideration has not been reported yet. We propose a fast method to detect pigs under various illumination conditions by exploiting the complementary information from depth and infrared images. By applying spatiotemporal interpolation, we first remove the noises caused by sunlight. Then, we carefully analyze the characteristics of both the depth and infrared information and detect pigs using only simple image processing techniques. Rather than exploiting highly time-consuming techniques, such as frequency-, optimization-, or deep learning-based detections, our image processing-based method can guarantee a fast execution time for the final goal, i.e., intelligent pig monitoring applications. In the experimental results, pigs could be detected effectively through the proposed method for both accuracy (i.e., 0.79) and execution time (i.e., 8.71 ms), even with various illumination conditions.

result.paraphrase: Rapid pig detection is a key requirement in a surveillance system aimed at continuously tracking individual pigs 24 h a day. In realistic pig-farm settings, varying lighting conditions such as sunlight must be taken into account, yet this has not been reported so far. We present a fast pig-detection method for diverse illumination conditions by leveraging the complementary information in depth and infrared images. Using spatiotemporal interpolation, we first eliminate sunlight-induced noise. We then examine the properties of both depth and infrared data and detect pigs with only simple image-processing methods. Instead of relying on time-consuming frequency-, optimization-, or deep learning-based approaches, our image-processing-based method ensures fast execution for the intended end use, namely intelligent pig-monitoring applications. Experimental results show that the proposed method detects pigs effectively under varied illumination, achieving 0.79 accuracy and 8.71 ms execution time.
